concepts.definition: The part of the program that collects the characters coming from the serial port and splits them into a command (letter) and a value (number).
concepts.example: The line W200 is decoded as 'forward, speed 200'.
concepts.pitfall: Trying to process the command before the line ending arrives; the buffer is only half full.

concepts.definition: A fixed-length array in which the incoming characters are collected until the line ends.
concepts.example: char tampon[12]; holds at most 11 characters; the last one is for '\0'.
concepts.pitfall: Not limiting the buffer: a long line overflows memory.

concepts.definition: atoi turns text into a whole number ("200" → 200), toupper turns a lower-case letter into upper case, and constrain squeezes a value into a range.
concepts.pitfall: Not limiting the speed: a silly value such as W9999 overflows analogWrite.

concepts.definition: The character that signals that the command has finished. 'Newline' must be selected in the Serial monitor.
concepts.example: If both \n and \r count as a line ending, the command is processed whichever setting is chosen.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing 'No line ending': the command is never completed and the robot does not react at all.

concepts.definition: This parser carries out a command until a new command arrives; it does not stop on its own.
concepts.example: If the connection drops after a single W150, the robot keeps going.
concepts.pitfall: Not taking this seriously: when the remote control drops out, the robot moves on out of control.

quiz.explanation: toupper turns the letter 'd' into 'D'. Because uzunluk is greater than 1, atoi(tampon + 1), that is "75", is read and the speed becomes 75. 150 is only used when no speed is written.

quiz.prompt: The command S-40 arrives at the parser. When hiz = constrain(atoi(tampon + 1), 0, 255) runs, what does hiz become?
quiz.explanation: atoi("-40") gives −40; because the lower limit of constrain is 0, the result is 0. The direction is chosen by the letter (S), not by the sign. The speed is never negative; thinking −40 would be a backward speed is wrong.

quiz.prompt: At PWM 150 each wheel turns in opposite directions at about 0.192 m/s (turning on the spot). L = 0.12 m. About how many seconds should the robot take to turn 180° (π rad)?
quiz.explanation: When turning on the spot, ω = 2·v / L = 2 · 0.192 / 0.12 = 3.2 rad/s. Time = π / 3.2, about 0.98 s. Using 2v instead of v (the wheels turn in opposite directions) doubles the turning speed.

options: The 'W' line: surus(hiz, hiz) is calculated wrongly
The 'W' line is missing a break; control falls through to the 'S' line and runs the motors backward
The 'S' line has an extra break
if should be used instead of switch
quiz.explanation: Because there is no break, the switch falls from the 'W' case into the 'S' case (fall-through); the second surus call overwrites the first and the robot goes backward. surus(hiz, hiz) is correct.

quiz.prompt: This week's serial command program is running. The operator sends a single W150 and the connection drops. What does the robot do?
options: It stops by itself after a few seconds
It keeps moving with the last command until a new command arrives
quiz.explanation: The pins stay the same until a command arrives; there is no timeout in the program. So the robot keeps going with the last command. This is a safety gap that will be closed with the watchdog in lesson 80.
